issues.description: Duplicate "transcriber_error" string in the message_type tuple
issues.detail: The tuple of error message types contains "transcriber_error" twice. This is harmless functionally (set-membership semantics via `in` on a tuple still works), but it is a code-readability defect: a careful reader will pause to ask whether the duplication is meaningful. Deduplicate, and consider promoting the literal set to a module-level frozenset named ERROR_MESSAGE_TYPES so the reader can see the catalog of errors in one place. UNDER-AUDITED / NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT.

issues.description: Loss of "WebSocket connection closed" diagnostic when the async-for terminates
issues.detail: The previous `_receive_messages` wrapped `_process_messages` in try/except and logged "WebSocket connection closed: {e}". After the refactor, the `async for message in self._get_websocket()` loop can still terminate (either by normal iteration end on close, or by an exception escaping the per-message try/except since the inner `except Exception` only covers JSON decode and processing errors — connection-level exceptions raised by the async iterator itself will now propagate). The diagnostic that previously told operators "connection closed, will reconnect" is gone. State the invariant: under what conditions does this coroutine return vs. raise, and is the outer reconnect loop in WebsocketService prepared for both? Add an explicit try/except around the async-for (logging then returning) or a literate comment documenting the contract with the caller. ASYMPTOTICALLY-OK-PRACTICALLY-UNDER-AUDITED.

issues.description: Error-type message handling lost per-type log context and labeled push_error prefix
issues.detail: Previously auth_error and quota_exceeded_error produced distinct logger.error lines ("ElevenLabs auth error: ...", "ElevenLabs quota exceeded: ...") and prefixed push_error with the category ("Auth error: ...", "Quota exceeded: ..."). The new collapsed branch emits only a generic "Error: ..." with no logger.error call at all for any of these categories — operators lose both the explicit log line and the categorization in the pushed frame. The fallback "Unknown error - {message_type}" is only used when `data.get("error")` is absent, so for real auth/quota errors the message_type never reaches logs or downstream. Add `logger.error(f"ElevenLabs {message_type}: {error_msg}")` and include message_type in the push_error prefix. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT.

`changelog/3233.fixed.md` ends without a newline ("\ No newline at end of file"). POSIX text-file convention and most tooling expect a trailing newline; concatenating changelog fragments will run lines together. Trivial fix.

issues.description: Magic list of error message types should be a named, documented constant
issues.detail: The catalog of fourteen error message_types lives inline in the `elif` branch. This is exactly the kind of literal where a literate-programming comment plus a named constant (e.g., `_ELEVENLABS_ERROR_MESSAGE_TYPES: frozenset[str] = frozenset({...})  # per https://elevenlabs.io/docs/.../error-handling`) pays for itself: the reader sees what set of conditions is being unified, where the list came from, and can audit it against the upstream docs without re-reading the dispatcher. Membership test becomes O(1) instead of O(n) on a 14-tuple — practically irrelevant here, but the readability win is real. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT.

review.summary: The change is small and the intent is sound: collapse a redundant try/except wrapper that was swallowing connection-closed exceptions and thereby preventing the outer reconnect loop from doing its job, and broaden the error-type dispatch to cover the full ElevenLabs error catalog. The algorithmic content is trivial — there is no real complexity or data-structure question here — so the audit reduces to readability, invariants, and information loss. Three concerns are worth addressing: (1) the error-type tuple contains a duplicate "transcriber_error" entry and should be promoted to a named, documented frozenset with a link to the upstream error-handling docs; (2) the per-type log lines (logger.error with "ElevenLabs auth error: ..." / "ElevenLabs quota exceeded: ...") and category prefixes on push_error were lost in the consolidation — operators will lose useful diagnostic categorization; (3) the deleted "WebSocket connection closed" log line removed a useful breadcrumb, and the new coroutine's termination contract with the reconnect loop is implicit rather than documented. None are correctness-fatal, but a literate-programming-grade comment plus the de-duplication and a restored log line would make this RIGOROUS instead of UNDER-AUDITED.
